subject: Mayor's Parking Enforcement Contract Approval
overview: The Council sharply critiqued the Mayor's decision to sign a parking enforcement contract with a private firm without further public hearings and debated a newly implemented tiered water rate system. Members also approved a new graffiti removal revolving account and addressed several infrastructure and public safety requests.

items.title: Graffiti Vandalism Revolving Account
items.summary: Approved the establishment of a revolving account for graffiti removal on public and private property. The resolution was amended to include the implementation of a smartphone reporting application and a request for a data report on local vandalism trends from the past 12 months.

items.title: Mayor's Parking Enforcement Contract and Public Safety
items.summary: Passed a resolution questioning the binding nature of concessions in the Mayor's new parking contract and requested a full copy of the signed agreement with Republic. Discussion focused on the lack of public hearings regarding the 'pay to park' plan and the need to prioritize a new police station over outsourced enforcement.

items.title: 2014 State Election Warrant
items.summary: Authorized the City Clerk to notify residents of the November 4, 2014, state election and confirmed the use of sixteen specific polling locations. The Clerk provided updates on ballot box maintenance and the availability of absentee ballots.

items.title: Cancellation of Meetings for Election and Veterans Day
items.summary: Approved the cancellation of the November 4 and November 11 council meetings due to the state election and the observance of Veterans Day.

items.title: Congratulatory Messages
items.summary: Approved resolutions sending congratulations to Assistant City Clerk Dorothy Donahue and residents Joan Gatto and Jean Entapa on the births of new grandchildren.

items.title: Dog Park Funding Itemization
items.summary: Requested a complete itemized list of donations and mitigation funds set aside for a city dog park. Members discussed the slow progress of the project since it was first proposed in 2011 and supported grassroots petition efforts to finalize a location.

items.title: Water and Sewer Rate Increases
items.summary: Referred the discussion of a new tiered water rate system to the Subcommittee on Auditing, Budget, and Finance. The Council expressed concern over the lack of public notice for the increase and questioned why rates are rising despite an $8.4 million surplus in the water and sewer account.

items.title: Public Safety Sidewalk Repairs
items.summary: Approved a request to replace hazardous sidewalks on Carolina Street following two trip-and-fall injuries. The motion was amended to include similar repairs for Yale Street, Main Street, and the corner of Winthrop and Badger Road.

items.title: National Disability Awareness Month Update
items.summary: Invited the Director of the Office on Disability to provide an update on city accessibility improvements and equal opportunity programming.

items.title: Public Participation on Police Personnel and Veteran Affairs
items.summary: Heard testimony from resident Jeanne Martin regarding police staffing levels, the need for community policing, and officer wellness programs. Martin also reported on the recent dedication of the Disabled Veterans for Life Memorial in Washington, D.C.
